# Rok Retar, mobile engineer

> Rok Retar is a mobile engineer in Slovenia who builds Android apps and takes Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) to production. He designed and led the move of a company's production iOS app onto shared Kotlin, keeping native UI where the platform does it better. He also builds Parrot, an ebook and audiobook reader for Android. This site is written in Kotlin with Kobweb. Below is a longer description of each page.

## Pages

### [Home](https://www.retar.app/)
Introduces Rok as an Android and Kotlin Multiplatform engineer. Covers how he works (share the domain and data layers, keep the UI native where the platform does it better, let module boundaries enforce dependency direction), the production iOS migration, his daily stack, the production apps he has shipped, the Parrot showcase and his engineering notes.

### [Parrot: ebook and audiobook reader](https://www.retar.app/parrot)
A case study for Parrot, a reader for your own ebooks and audiobooks on Android phones, tablets and e-ink readers, built with Kotlin Multiplatform. Features: read-along highlighting for ebooks with synced narration, on-device voices that read any ebook aloud, one reading position across the ebook and audiobook versions of a book, Storyteller, Audiobookshelf and OPDS libraries, Parrot Cloud, highlights, notes and an offline dictionary, an e-ink theme, and reading statistics. The page links the latest APK and the full version history.

### [Wrapping the AppsFlyer SDK into a Kotlin Multiplatform library](https://www.retar.app/blog/appsflyer-kmp-wrapper)
An engineering note on wrapping the native AppsFlyer Android and iOS SDKs behind one coroutine-first Kotlin API with expect/actual, two native delegates and no callbacks.

### [Building a smooth, infinite carousel in Kobweb](https://www.retar.app/blog/infinite-carousel)
An engineering note on implementing a smooth, infinite carousel component in Kobweb using Compose for Web. Covers the technique for seamless looping, performance considerations, and the Compose-level API design.

### [Shipping SQLCipher inside a static Kotlin/Native framework](https://www.retar.app/blog/sqlcipher-static-kotlin-native-framework)
An engineering note on embedding SQLCipher into a static Kotlin/Native framework for iOS. Covers the build configuration, linking challenges, and how to ship encrypted SQLite in a KMP shared module that compiles to a static framework for iOS consumption.

## About

Rok Retar is a mobile engineer based in Slovenia. He writes business logic, data layers and domain models once in Kotlin and shares them between Android and iOS; the domain layer depends on nothing, and module structure enforces it. Besides the iOS migration, he has shipped an AI platform with real-time chat, timelines and push notifications, a gaming app with NFC, biometric sign-in, cashless payments and white-label builds, and Parrot.

Daily stack: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Compose Multiplatform, Ktor, Koin, Decompose, SQLDelight with SQLCipher, SKIE for Swift interop, and Kobweb for the web.

Open to senior mobile engineering roles, Kotlin Multiplatform migrations and Android architecture work, remote across the EU.

## Technology

This site is built natively in Kotlin with Kobweb, which brings a Compose-like developer experience to the web via Kotlin/JS. Analytics are privacy-friendly via Umami (no cookies, no PII). No third-party trackers beyond Umami are used.
